scope.q: What specific customer interaction data (e.g., support tickets, product usage, billing changes) do you currently collect and have readily accessible for analysis?
scope.why: Understanding available data sources is critical to determine what signals can actually be used to predict churn and avoid building on assumptions.

scope.q: Beyond just 'a reason,' what level of detail and interpretability do success managers require from the churn prediction model to actually trust and act on its output?
scope.why: The definition of 'trust' and 'reason' is subjective; clarifying this prevents delivering a solution that is technically sound but practically unusable.

scope.q: What is the acceptable false positive rate for churn predictions, considering the cost of unnecessary outreach versus the cost of a missed churn?
scope.why: Defining an acceptable error tolerance is crucial for model calibration and for managing expectations around the model's practical utility and impact on workflow.

decomposition.title: Data Ingestion & Harmonization
decomposition.why: Raw data from various sources needs to be collected, cleaned, and standardized into a unified format for effective feature engineering.

decomposition.title: Feature Engineering & Selection
decomposition.why: Relevant predictive features must be extracted or constructed from the harmonized data to capture patterns indicative of churn.

decomposition.title: Churn Prediction Model Training
decomposition.why: A machine learning model needs to be trained on historical data to learn the relationship between features and customer churn.

decomposition.title: Model Interpretability & Explanation Generation
decomposition.why: A mechanism is required to explain *why* a customer is predicted to churn, providing the 'reason' success managers need for trust.

decomposition.title: Prediction & Alerting Service
decomposition.why: The trained model must be deployed to generate real-time or batch predictions and trigger alerts for success managers.

sprint.title: Data Ingestion MVP
sprint.deliv: Connect to 2 key data sources (e.g., CRM, usage logs) and ingest into a staging area.

sprint.title: Initial Feature Engineering & Baseline Model
sprint.deliv: Generate 5-10 baseline features; train a simple logistic regression churn model and evaluate initial metrics.

sprint.title: Model Interpretability Prototype
sprint.deliv: Integrate a basic interpretability library (e.g., LIME/SHAP) to generate explanations for individual predictions.

sprint.title: Prediction Service & Alerting
sprint.deliv: Deploy the model and explanation service as an API endpoint, trigger email alerts for high-churn predictions.

sprint.title: Success Manager Dashboard MVP
sprint.deliv: Build a basic dashboard displaying churn predictions, top reasons, and customer details for a sample set of customers.

risks.risk: Insufficient historical churn data or poor data quality prevents effective model training.
risks.mitigation: Conduct a thorough data audit upfront to assess data availability and quality; if lacking, explore alternative data collection or proxy metrics.

risks.risk: Generated explanations are not understandable or actionable for success managers, leading to low adoption.
risks.mitigation: Involve success managers early in the explanation design process through mockups and iterative feedback sessions to ensure utility and clarity.

risks.risk: Model predictions have a high false positive rate, overwhelming success managers with non-churning customers.
risks.mitigation: Implement adjustable confidence thresholds for alerting, allow success managers to provide feedback on prediction accuracy, and continuously retrain with new data.

risks.risk: Data privacy or security concerns with centralizing customer data for ML training and predictions.
risks.mitigation: Establish clear data governance policies, implement robust access controls, and anonymize/pseudonymize sensitive data where possible.
